title: A MAN WITH A DRAWN SWORD

memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text: Now when Joshua was near Jericho, he looked up and saw a man standing in front of him with a drawn sword in his hand. Joshua went up to him and asked, "Are you for us or for our enemies?" — Josh 5:13 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
As Joshua surveys the great fortress of Jericho, he suddenly sees a man standing before him with a drawn sword. It is a startling, holy moment. Joshua, ever the soldier, asks the natural question: "Are you for us or for our enemies?" He wants to know which side this warrior is on.

There is something instructive in Joshua's question, and in the answer he is about to receive. We tend to approach God the way Joshua first approached this figure — asking whether God is on our side, whether He will back our plans and our causes. But that is often the wrong question. The real question is not whether God is on our side, but whether we are on His.

Joshua was about to learn that this was no ordinary man, and that the more important issue was not recruiting God to Joshua's mission, but Joshua submitting to God's mission. God does not exist to serve our agenda; we exist to serve His.

This is a healthy reset for all of us. In our prayers and plans, are we mainly asking God to bless what we have decided, or are we asking to be aligned with what God is doing? Jesus taught us to pray, "your will be done" (Matt 6:10), not "my will be done." The question is not "Is God for me?" but "Am I for God?" That shift changes everything.

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
1. Do you tend to ask God to join your plans, or ask to join His?
2. In your prayers, is it more "my will be done" or "Your will be done"?
3. What would change if you sought to be on God's side rather than getting Him on yours?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text: Lord, forgive me for trying to recruit You to my plans. Help me instead to align my life with Your will and to say, "Your will be done." Amen.
